----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
 ORDER (09/09/2019) This petition has been filed by the petitioner under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for quashing of the proceedings of Criminal Case No.2735/2011 pending before the Court of Judicial Magistrate First Class, Chhindwara wherein the petitioner is facing trial under Section 59 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 [for short "2006 Act"] read with Section 50 of Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules (hereinafter referred to as the "Rules").
2.

entities.text: Court of Judicial Magistrate First Class, Chhindwara
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Heard both the learned counsel for the parties at length and perused the record.
3. Learned counsel for the petitioner contended that without adding the manufacturer as a party, the case against the present petitioner is not maintainable.
He further alleged that, after repeal of the earlier Act viz Preservation of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 the petitioner cannot be prosecuted for the offence in this regard.
4. Learned Panel Lawyer for the respondent/State has strongly opposed the aforesaid contention of the petitioner.

5. In this regard, it is important to mention here that the charge under Section 59 of the Food Safety Vijay Gugnani vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 9 September, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/110256708/
1 and Standards Act, 2006 has been framed against the petitioner on 11.11.2011.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thereafter, the case was continuously adjourned at the stage of prosecution evidence.
The petitioner has not challenged the aforesaid order dated 11.11.2011 anywhere, whereby he has been charged under Section 59 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.

6. In the said order, learned trial Court clearly held that since the earlier Act was repealed, therefore,
charge has been framed under Section 59 of the Act, because there is allegations against the petitioner that he had stored Haldiram Milk Bread for sale, which was found misbranded.

Hence,
charge has rightly been framed by the trial Court.
7. It is also found in the record that the complaint has been filed after receiving the sanction for prosecution from the Competent Officer against the petitioner.
Hence, the objections raised by the petitioner are not sustainable.

8. Further that Section 89 of the 2006 Act prescribes as under:-
"89.

Overriding effect of this Act over all other food related laws- The provisions of this Act shall have effect notwithstanding anything inconsistent therewith contained in any other law for the time being in force or in any instrument having effect by virtue of any law other than this Act."
9.
Thus, this Court comes to the conclusion that the petitioner has rightly been prosecuted by the trial Court under Section 59 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.

10. In the light of principles laid down by the Supreme Court in the cases of Mukund Das Maheshwari Vs. State of M.P. [M.Cr.C. No.10644/2006 decided on 30.03.2017], Managing Director Vs. State of M.P. [M.Cr.C. No.1301/2011 decided on 20.02.2017] and Sharad Kumar Sanghi Vs.
Sangita Rane, (2015) 12 SCC 781.

sentences.text: The manufacturer is a necessary party.
Hence, it is directed that the complainant shall make the Manufacturer Company of the food item as respondent No.2 in the proceedings within fifteen days, then notice be issued to it.
Thereafter, trial Court shall proceed according to law for the offence committed by them under Section 59 of the Food Safety and standards Act, 2006.
11. With the aforesaid direction, this petition stands disposed of.

12. Let record of the trial Court be sent back immediately along with the copy of this order.
